title: Which kind of selectivity?
caption: When a reaction could give more than one product, ask what the products differ in. Reaction at one functional group rather than another is chemoselectivity; at one position rather than another, regioselectivity; one stereoisomer rather than another, stereoselectivity.
alt: A tree: do the possible products differ in which functional group reacted? Chemoselective. If not, in where on the molecule? Regioselective. Otherwise in 3D arrangement: stereoselective.
description: Different functional group reacted: chemoselective, such as NaBH₄ reducing a ketone but not an ester.
Same group, different position: regioselective, such as HBr giving 2-bromopropane from propene.
Same connections, different 3D arrangement: stereoselective, such as anti addition of Br₂.

q1.q: Do the products differ in which functional group reacted?

q2.q: Do they differ in where on the molecule?
